case_name: P.V. George & Ors v State Of Kerala & Ors
facts: The Government of Kerala framed rules for the employees of Kerala Government Presses Subordinate Services to which cadre the appellants belonged.
Appellants were working in the Government Presses, Kerala.
A further proviso was appended thereto by a Government order dated 30.08.1984 in term of SRO No. 1044 of 1984.

Constitutionality of the said provision was challenged before the Kerala High Court, whereupon a Division Bench thereof in Daniel v. State of Kerala [1985 KLT 1057], declared the same to be ultra vires.
The correctness of the said decision was questioned before another Division Bench of the said Court in Writ Appeal No. 149 of 1990.
issues: Application of the doctrine of prospective overruling in service matters
petitioner_arguments: The High Court committed a manifest error insofar as it failed to take into consideration that in service matters ordinarily doctrine of prospective overruling would apply.

Reliance has been placed on Managing Director ECIL, Hyderabad v. B. Karunakar [(1993) 4 SCC 727 1993 Indlaw SC 430], R.K. Sabharwal v. State of Punjab [(1995) 2 SCC 745 1995 Indlaw SC 1756], Union of India and Others v. Virpal Singh Chauhan and Others [(1995) 6 SCC 684 1995 Indlaw SC 1803], Ashok Kumar Gupta v. State of U.P. [(1997) 5 SCC 201 1997 Indlaw SC 1096], Ajit Singh-II v. State of Punjab [(1999) 7 SCC 209 1999 Indlaw SC 725], Baburam v. C.C. Jacob [(1999) 3 SCC 362 1999 Indlaw SC 274], E.A. Sathyanesan v. V.K. Agnihotri and Others [(2004) 9 SCC 165 2003 Indlaw SC 1426], M. Nagaraj & Others v. Union of India & Others [(2006)10 SCALE 301 2006 Indlaw SC 722].
respondent_arguments: The judgment was supported by Mr. Uday U. Lalit, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents.
court_reasoning: This Court in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 32 or Article 142 of the Constitution of India may declare a law to have a prospective effect.

The Division Bench of the High Court may be correct in opining that having regard to the decision of this Court in L.C. Golak Nath and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [AIR 1967 SC 1643 1967 Indlaw SC 1493) the power of overruling is vested only in this Court and that too in constitutional matters, but the High Courts in exercise of their jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, even without applying the doctrine of prospective overruling, indisputably may grant a limited relief in exercise of their equity jurisdiction.
holding: The judgments appealed against are confirmed. The writ appeals are dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.
